headline: India's peak power demand drops to 234 GW as cooling needs ease
hook: Cooler weather relieves high grid pressure
summary: India's peak power demand has declined to around 234 GW from over 250 GW in early October, driven by cooler weather and rainfall. Consumption had previously surged to a record 260 GW on October 5 due to below-normal monsoon rains, keeping short-term power exchange prices above ₹7 per unit. While national demand is easing, states like Gujarat and Tamil Nadu continue to register high demand from weather and industrial loads. Domestic coal stocks at power plants stood at 17.3 million tonnes as of October 24, down slightly from earlier in the month.
why_it_matters: Spot power exchange prices may cool as electricity demand drops.
winners_losers: Power consumers gain / short-term power traders hurt
